sample.question:
Pipeworks is a plumbing puzzle. The board is a grid of square tiles; rows are numbered from 0 at the top downward and columns from 0 at the left rightward, so a tile is written (row, column). Each tile either holds a fixed pipe piece (straight, elbow, T-junction or cross) or is empty. A pipe piece has openings on some sides of its tile; water can pass between two adjacent tiles only when BOTH tiles have pipe openings on their shared edge. The blue PUMP outside the board pushes water into the tile it points at, through that tile's edge on the board rim; if that tile has no opening on that edge, no water enters at all. Lettered buckets outside the board are outlets: an outlet receives water when the rim tile it touches gets filled AND that tile has an opening on the touching edge. Water spreads through every connected opening (it can branch at T-junctions and crosses).

The pump is attached to the bottom edge of the board and feeds tile (5, 4); outlet A sits below the bottom edge, touching tile (5, 1); outlet B sits right of the right edge, touching tile (0, 5); outlet C sits right of the right edge, touching tile (5, 5).
When the pump is switched on, how many tiles of the grid end up filled with water? Answer with a single number.
sample.analysis:
Trace the water flow step by step:
Water enters at tile (5, 4) through its south opening (a cross pipe (openings: north-east-south-west)).
From (5, 4) water flows east into (5, 5) (a T-junction pipe (openings: north-east-west)).
From (5, 4) water flows west into (5, 3) (a T-junction pipe (openings: north-east-west)).
From (5, 3) water flows west into (5, 2) (a T-junction pipe (openings: north-east-west)).
From (5, 2) water flows north into (4, 2) (an elbow pipe (openings: east-south)).
Tile (5, 5) is wet and has a east opening on the board edge, so outlet C receives water.
The filled tiles, in filling order, are: (5, 4), (5, 5), (5, 3), (5, 2), (4, 2).
Counting them gives 5 tiles.
So the answer is 5.
